1. Petitioner claiming to be a public spirited citizen is knocking at the doors of this Writ Court in PIL jurisdiction for the quashment of 2nd respondent - Deputy Commissioner's order dated 18.02.2021 at Annexure-M whereby, a piece, in all, 8 acres & 25 guntas of land is directed to be bought for the construction of Mini Vidhan Soudha in Holasur of Bidar District.
He also calls in question another order dated 27.10.2021 made by the said Deputy Commissioner at Annexure-P whereby, his request for rescinding the above dated 18.02.2021 has been rejected.

Learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner vehemently argues that, there is absolutely no reason for the State to buy certain private land at the cost of public exchequer when his client is ready and willing to gift 3 acres of land in the vicinity.
Therefore, he seeks a writ of mandamus to the official respondents to accept the land freely tendered.

After service of notice, the respondents have entered appearance through the learned Additional Government Advocate who opposes the petition contending that what land is suitable for the construction of Mini Vidhan Soudha is for the Authority to decide and that a private citizen cannot meddle with such decision; although the Government in exercise of the power of Eminent Domain can compulsorily acquire private land for public purpose, it cannot be directed to accept free presentation of land from the citizen.
Therefore, she contends, there being no justiciable right which can be enforced by the Writ Court in PIL jurisdiction.
So contending she seeks dismissal of the writ petition.
3. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the papers, we decline indulgence in the matter broadly agreeing with the submission of AGA appearing for the respondents.
Where a structure like Mini Vidhan Soudha should be erected is ordinarily falls within the Executive Domain and Courts cannot run a race of NC: 2023:KHC:33302-DB opinions with the Authorities.

It hardly needs to be stated that the doctrine of separation of powers being an essential feature of the Constitution, the organs of the State have to show mutual difference to the decisions taken by the respective branches.

If the Authorities in their wisdom have chosen a particular land for constructing a public structure of some significance, the Courts cannot undertake a deeper examination of such decisions, unless legal infirmities obtaining therein are demonstrated from the record.

4. The vehement submission of learned Senior Advocate appearing for the petitioner that when a citizen is ready and willing to gift his property for a public purpose, the Authorities cannot refuse to take the same, is bit difficult to countenance.

Right to property is constitutionally guarantee under Article 300A and the corresponding duty not to curtail that right subject to all just exceptions lies on Sri Vishwanathappa A Khadadi vs The State Of Karnataka on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133827800/
3 the shoulders of the Government.

sentences.text:
A private property cannot be taken away by the State NC:
2023:KHC:33302-DB except in due process of law, namely, for the public purpose and ordinarily on payment of compensation vide K T PLANTATION PVT. LTD. vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA, (2011) 9 SCC 1.

entities.text: K T PLANTATION PVT. LTD. vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA, (2011) 9 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, no rule or ruling is cited before us to substantiate the contention that if a citizen wants to give his property free of cost for a particular purpose, the Government has to accept the same.

Section 122 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 defines Gift as "the transfer of certain existing movable or immovable property made voluntarily and without consideration, by one person, called the donor, to another, called the donee, and accepted by or on behalf of the donee."
For a transfer fructify as a gift, this provision prescribes the acceptance as a sine qua non.
There is nothing in the said provision which mandates the acceptance.

5. It hardly needs to be stated that the power of the Government to take private property for public purpose on payment of compensation is one thing and compelling the Government to take a private property even if freely offered, is another.

The power of Eminent Domain is NC:
2023:KHC:33302-DB constitutionally recognized in the provisions of Article 300A which permits acquisition of private property for public purpose.

The Apex Court has observed that a Government cannot be compelled to acquire private property and therefore, a writ petition seeking such a direction is misconceived vide PRAKASH AMICHAND SHAH vs. STATE OF GUJARAT, (1986) 1 SCC 581.

entities.text: PRAKASH AMICHAND SHAH vs. STATE OF GUJARAT, (1986) 1 SCC 581
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, this petition being devoid of merits is liable to be and accordingly dismissed, costs having been made easy.

Nothing observed hereinabove shall come in the way of petitioner gifting his property for public or charitable use to any person, body of individuals, associations, societies or the like, if he is so desires.
